Myopia vs Hypermetropia: does near-sighted mean near things look blurry? It is the opposite. Class 10 Physics, The Human Eye.

• Myopia (near-sightedness): near is clear, far is blurry. The image of a distant object forms in front of the retina
• Cause: too much curvature of the eye lens, or an elongated eyeball. Fix: a concave lens
• Hypermetropia (far-sightedness): far is clear, near is blurry. Rays from a near object focus behind the retina
• Cause: focal length too long, or the eyeball too small. Fix: a convex lens
